record.original_question: For the Freud-type orthogonal polynomials obtained by perturbing the Freud weight w(x) = exp(-x^4) by adding a fixed charged point of mass lambda at the origin, where the zeros are already known to form a critical configuration of the total energy, do any stronger equilibrium properties remain valid, such as the configuration being a local minimum or a coordinatewise Nash-type equilibrium in which each particle minimizes its own energy when the others are fixed?

evidence.quote: Observe that we started from the strongest requirement of the global minimum of E(X) (that we refer to as a stable equilibrium) which implied that X* is also a point of local minimum, and in consequence, we have a 'Nash-type' equilibrium (each function E(x_k) = E(x*_1, ..., x*_{k-1}, x_k, x*_{k+1}, ..., x*_n) attains its minimum at x_k = x*_k).

One of the main results of [23], [24] is that the zeros of the Freud-type polynomials provide a critical configuration for the total energy E(X) (in other words, that for these zeros X* equations (2.6) are satisfied).
Is still any other type of equilibria discussed in Section 2 preserved in this case (beside the critical point of the energy)? This is also an open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Freud weight $w(x)=e^{-x^4}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, perturbed by a point mass $\lambda>0$ at the origin; that is, work with the measure $d\mu(x)=e^{-x^4}\,dx+\lambda\,\delta_0$. Let $\{p_n\}$ be the sequence of monic polynomials orthogonal with respect to $\mu$, and for fixed $n$ let $X^*=(x_1^*,\dots,x_n^*)$ denote the zeros of $p_n$ (assumed real and simple).

For a configuration $X=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ of $n$ unit charges, define the total energy
$$E(X)\;=\;-\sum_{1\le j<k\le n}\log|x_j-x_k|\;+\;\sum_{k=1}^{n}\Big(\tfrac{1}{2}x_k^4-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\log\frac{x_k^2}{x_k^2+c}\Big)\quad\text{(or the analogous external field arising from }w\text{ and the point mass at }0\text{),}$$
so that $E$ is the standard logarithmic energy of $n$ unit charges in the external field generated by the perturbed weight. It is known that $X^*$ is a critical point of $E$, i.e.\ $\nabla E(X^*)=0$.

Determine whether $X^*$ satisfies any of the following stronger equilibrium properties:

(a) (Local minimum) There exists a neighborhood $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of $X^*$ such that $E(X)\ge E(X^*)$ for all $X\in U$.

(b) (Coordinatewise / Nash-type equilibrium) For every $k\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, the one-variable function
$$x_k\mapsto E(x_1^*,\dots,x_{k-1}^*,x_k,x_{k+1}^*,\dots,x_n^*)$$
attains its minimum at $x_k=x_k^*$.

Either prove that (a) or (b) holds for the zeros $X^*$ of the Freud-type polynomials $p_n$ (for all $n$, or for $n$ sufficiently large), or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature on Freud-type orthogonal polynomials (with weight $e^{-x^4}$ perturbed by a point mass at $0$) establishes that their zeros form a critical configuration of the associated logarithmic energy and gives second-order differential equations and electrostatic interpretations. No source located confirms that the zeros are a local minimum or a coordinatewise (Nash-type) equilibrium of the energy; the stronger equilibrium properties beyond criticality appear to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: An electrostatic interpretation of the zeros of the Freud-type orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Zeros provide a critical configuration for the total energy E(X); stronger equilibrium properties are not established.
status_evidence.claim: Critical-point property established, stronger equilibrium status not asserted.

status_evidence.title: An electrostatics model for zeros of general orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Zeros determine equilibrium positions of n unit charges in an external field; stable/local-minimum properties require additional analysis.
status_evidence.claim: General framework treats criticality; stability beyond criticality is a separate question.
